newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CYCLING-MENGIN GIVES NEW FRENCH TEAM FIRST TOUR STAGE WIN.
newsitem.headline: CYCLING-MENGIN GIVES NEW FRENCH TEAM FIRST TOUR STAGE WIN.

text.p: French cyclocross champion Christophe Mengin gave the new Francaise des Jeux team their first stage win in the Tour de France on Tuesday.

Mengin won the sprint in the Swiss city of Fribourg at the end of the 181-km 16th stage from Morzine in the French Alps with Belgian Franck Vandenbroucke second and compatriot Richard Virenque, second overall, third.
Germany's Jan Ullrich, finishing in the same time of four hours 30 minutes 11 seconds, retained the overall leader's yellow jersey and his advantage of 6:22 over Virenque.
Defending champion Bjarne Riis had an unhappy day, dropping from fourth to seventh overall after struggling in the mountains and coming in 6:12 adrift.
The Dane is 18:07 behind and just over eight minutes behind third-placed Italian Marco Pantani, at the start of the stage his chief rival for a place on the podium in Paris on Sunday.
Spaniard Fernando Escartin and Abraham Olano and Francesco Casagrande of Italy have moved above Riis in the standings.
Mengin, third in the world amateur championship in 1994, said: "This was a friends' victory by the whole Francaise des Jeux team.

"We were looking for a stage victory since we are not well placed overall as a team. I know I can go fast so I knew I had my chances," said Mengin, a former carpenter on his second Tour after previously riding for Casino.
"I had good legs when I saw I was holding my own, notably against Riis. I realised I was on a good day."
Mengin dedicated his win to his infant daughter Tessie. "She was two on the 16th of July and I wanted to give her a win then. Well, it was today instead."
Last Wednesday's 11th stage was similar, also ending with a long downhill finish after leaving the Pyrenees.
Riis struggled after being left for dead on the long haul up the second of three climbs at Col de la Croix.
Spaniard Aitor Garmendia, who had made a break with a small group including Mengin's French team mate Stephane Heulot and Colombia's Chepe Gonzalez, reached the summit first.
A group including Ullrich, Virenque and Pantani chased them, although at one point they were three minutes behind.
But Riis, suffering from a concerted attack by Pantani's Mercatone Uno team, failed to live with their pace and dropped more than seven minutes behind.
Garmendia and Heulot went out ahead on their own on the third climb to Col des Mosses.
But on the long 66-km descent to Fribourg they were eventually absorbed by the first group at Bulle 28 kms from the finish where Heulot handed over to Mengin.
Ullrich brushed aside suggestions the Tour was over as a contest, saying: "There are still five days to go. I'm glad things went so well in the mountains.
"Today was not my best day, my legs hurt a bit and I had a small throat problem, but very slight," said the 23-year-old German who spoke to reporters with a towel wrapped tightly round his neck.
The Tour returns to France on Wednesday with the 218.5-km 17th stage, including three middle-range climbs in the first half and an 80-km downhill run to the finish at Colmar.
